name: Nadir Frost
description: Nadir Frost exists at the frigid nadir of its star system, orbiting so far from its sun that the star appears as merely the brightest point in the sky. Nitrogen ice covers the plains in smooth, reflective sheets that crack and refreeze in slow geological cycles. Methane frost accumulates on the mountain peaks in thick, white deposits that sublimate directly to gas during the brief thermal maximum, only to re-deposit when the temperature drops again.

The thin atmosphere is mostly nitrogen with traces of methane and carbon monoxide, barely enough to scatter the feeble starlight into a pale grey sky. Sound travels poorly in the tenuous air, and the world exists in a profound silence broken only by the occasional groan of shifting ice. The cold is absolute, a fundamental condition of existence rather than a temporary state, and it permeates every surface and crevice.

Cryogenic canyon systems cut through the nitrogen ice plains, carved by some ancient process that may have involved the flow of liquid nitrogen during a warmer epoch in the planet's history. The canyon walls reveal layered ice strata of different compositions, a frozen geological record that spans billions of years. Analysis of these layers has provided insights into the star system's thermal history and the gradual cooling that relegated Nadir Frost to its current frozen state.

Nadir Frost serves primarily as a scientific outpost and navigational waypoint for expeditions to the outer system. Its nitrogen ice deposits are a convenient source of reaction mass for spacecraft, and a small automated refueling station operates on the largest plain. The extreme cold presents ongoing maintenance challenges, as even hardened equipment succumbs to material brittleness at these temperatures.
